Findings

1. "The scenes", scene 4 (Coming in), line 161, the last sentence (change 8). A carrier keeps its patient whatever the stored position does (line 115), so a den made on a carrier patient's five-thing cart can be followed by a door patient laid out at `bowl`, whose cart carries the bowl alone (line 100); there the sentence puts the blanket on a cart that does not carry it, against "each thing the new cart carries lies on the cart again" in the same line.
   Now: "`made` is not changed, and what was made of a thing comes in with it, but for a den whose basket the new cart does not carry: that den is taken apart, and the blanket lies on the cart."
   Replace with: "`made` is not changed, and what was made of a thing comes in with it, but for a den whose basket the new cart does not carry: that den is taken apart, and the blanket lies on the cart if the new cart carries it."

2. "The scenes", scene 3 (The mouse's showing), line 160, the sentence in brackets (change 2). With the bowl "never shown", the scene's own cause (a cart "carrying a thing the mouse has not shown") holds at every coming in, and every patient that droops breaks line 111 ("A patient is never laid out with a need whose thing the mouse has not yet shown"); the bowl has to count as shown, in the words line 112 already uses.
   Now: "The mouse uses it on itself the right way (wraps a corner of the blanket round itself, brushes its whiskers, sticks a plaster on its tail, curls up in the basket and breathes out; the bowl lies alone on the first cart and is never shown)."
   Replace with: "The mouse uses it on itself the right way (wraps a corner of the blanket round itself, brushes its whiskers, sticks a plaster on its tail, curls up in the basket and breathes out; the bowl has no showing: at the first position it lies alone on the cart and fits, and at every position it counts as shown)."
